problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y={x}^{2}-6x$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $3\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=2\,\text{cm}.$
worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={x}^{2}-6x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}-6x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-6x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2x-6).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3\,\text{cm}/\text{s}$ and $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =3\cdot (2\cdot 2-6)\,\text{cm}/\text{s} \\  & =-6\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$
